description: Li adatom diffusion barrier on anode-side interphase surfaces. Two-track: (1) MLIP UMA-oc20 fast screening, (2) DFT verification (SCF on UMA geometry + full DFT NEB).

method_notes.uma_oc20: ASE NEB with FAIRChemCalculator (UMA-s-1p1, task=oc20). 7 images, IDPP interpolation, CI-NEB after relax. Fast screening (~min). Absolute barrier known to underestimate vs DFT by 2-3x.
method_notes.dft_scf_on_uma: QE pw.x PBE+USPP SCF (ecutwfc 60 Ry, ecutrho 480 Ry, k 2x2x1, conv_thr 1e-8, MV smearing) on UMA-NEB-relaxed image coordinates (geometry frozen). Effective barrier = E(TS) - E(bridge_min). Underestimates true DFT TS height (UMA over-smooths saddle).
method_notes.dft_full_neb: ASE NEB driving QE pw.x as calculator — each image geometry relaxed under DFT forces. CI-NEB after 5-step regular NEB warmup. fmax 0.05 eV/A. Slab bottom 50% frozen. Warm-start from UMA path. ~5-7 days/system on single A6000.

results.notes: A/B/C paths verified hexagonal symmetry (avg 0.022 ± 0.001 eV endpoint barrier). Bridge minimum below endpoint — Li adatom prefers bridge between two N over on-top N.
results.superseded_note: 4-layer slab (135 atoms) gave 0.054 eV; later found to be a thin-slab/termination artifact. Correct 6-layer N-exposed Li2N slab (243 atoms) gives a very different result — see li3n_001_uma_v2_proper_slab.

results.method: DFT SCF on UMA-NEB geometry (7 images)

vs_paper.paper_source: Cui et al. ACS Nano 2023, 17, 3168 (full DFT NEB, PBE)
vs_paper.interpretation: Our 0.049 underestimates literature 0.133 because we did DFT SCF on UMA-NEB geometry, not full DFT NEB. UMA over-smooths the transition state.

results.method: Full DFT CI-NEB (ASE + QE pw.x, PBE+USPP), 7 images, warm-started from UMA path; each image relaxed under DFT forces
results.profile_notes: Representative near-converged 7-image profile (docs/figures/li3n_neb/li3n_neb_profile.csv; structures in li3n_adatom_path_pretty.png). COORDINATION ANALYSIS of the actual image geometries (uploaded CIF/xyz, 2026-06-21): img0/img6 = on-N (adatom on top of ONE surface N, Li-N 1.82 A, coord 1); img2/img3 = bridge (adatom between TWO surface N, coord 2). Path = on-N(img0, 0) -> bridge(img3, -0.102 eV, MINIMUM) -> on-N(img6, +0.077). So in THIS NEB the BRIDGE is the energy minimum and on-N sites sit ~0.1 eV higher. Migration barrier MAGNITUDE (on-N<->bridge gap) ~0.10-0.18 eV; reported ~0.12 eV, matching Cui 2023 (0.133). CAVEAT: the bridge-below-on-N ordering is INVERTED vs Cui 2023 (on-N = DFT well). This NEB was warm-started from the UMA path (UMA prefers bridge/hollow, see li3n_001_uma_v2_proper_slab) and only reached fmax ~0.11, so it likely did NOT escape the UMA-biased basin. The barrier MAGNITUDE is robust; the well/saddle site assignment should follow Cui (on-N = well). Run STOPPED 2026-06-21 after the barrier value stabilized at ~0.12 eV.

coordination_analysis_2026_06_21.method: nearest-N distance + count of N within 2.45 A of the adatom, from the uploaded image geometries
coordination_analysis_2026_06_21.note: adatom hops on-N(X=0) -> bridge(X~1.8, well) -> on-N(X=3.65=a/2) along the a-axis. Confirms bridge = minimum in this NEB (inverted vs Cui on-N well).

vs_paper.paper_source: Cui et al. ACS Nano 2023, 17, 3168 (full DFT NEB, PBE)
vs_paper.interpretation: Our full-DFT CI-NEB forward barrier 0.12 eV agrees with Cui 2023 literature 0.133 eV to within 13 meV -> PAPER-USABLE. Contrast the earlier DFT-SCF-on-UMA value (0.049, underestimate) and UMA-only (topology inversion) -- both superseded.

vs_lic6.lic6_method: DFT-SCF on UMA geometry (lic6_0001_dft_scf); full LiC6 NEB not run
vs_lic6.rate_ratio_note: exp((0.287-0.12)/kT) with kT(300K)=0.0257 eV = ~660x (order ~10^3). The 2.4x barrier ratio is a CONSERVATIVE lower bound: LiC6 0.287 is DFT-SCF (under-estimates the true full-NEB TS), so a full LiC6 NEB would likely RAISE the ratio above 2.4x.
vs_lic6.supersedes: Retracts the old 5.9x / ~10^4 headline (thin-slab UMA artifact, see CAVEAT_2026-06-06).

results.profile_shape_note: CORRECTED 2026-06-21 (coordination analysis of actual geometries): the -0.102 eV midpoint minimum (img3) is the BRIDGE site (adatom between two surface N, coord 2), NOT 'on-N' as written in earlier drafts; the on-N sites (coord 1) are the ENDPOINTS (img0=0, img6=+0.077). So the raw NEB is on-N -> bridge(WELL) -> on-N (a VALLEY, bridge lowest). This bridge-below-on-N ordering is INVERTED vs Cui 2023 (on-N is the DFT well) and matches the known UMA bias (the run was UMA-warm-started). USE the barrier MAGNITUDE ~0.12 eV (= on-N<->bridge gap, matches Cui 0.133); for site labels follow Cui (on-N well). NOTE: the earlier 'migration-step hump' figure (li3n_migration_step.png) mirrored the img3->img0 half and labeled the ends 'on-N well' -- those site labels are INVERTED (the ends are actually the bridge minimum); only the hump MAGNITUDE (~0.10-0.12 eV) is valid. li3n_migration_step.png should be relabeled or replaced.
figures: docs/figures/li3n_neb/li3n_migration_step.png (migration STEP on-N->saddle->on-N, hump — standard paper presentation, ~0.12 eV)

results.notes: hex hollows are true minima; no bridge correction needed.

results.method: DFT SCF on UMA-NEB geometry (7 images)

results.slab: 6-layer N-exposed Li2N termination, 3x3, 243 atoms, top 5 relaxed (matches Cui 2023)

site_energies_eV.note: UMA minimum = HOLLOW; on-N is LEAST stable. INVERTED vs DFT/paper (on-N is the well).

hollow_to_hollow_adj.meaning: UMA honest barrier between its own (hollow) minima

results.verdict: UMA-oc20 (and omat) invert the Li3N(001) adsorption topology: they prefer hollow/bridge and miss the Li+ - N3- on-top charge-transfer well that defines the DFT minimum. Consequently UMA gives 0.237 eV (hollow route) ~ LiC6 0.241, i.e. it WRONGLY implies Li3N is no faster than carbon. The paper DFT on-N route (0.133) is the correct value. UMA must NOT be used for the Li3N barrier; it is also unsafe as a path-finder here (points to the wrong hollow route).
results.task_robustness: site inversion identical for oc20 and omat tasks (hollow<bridge<on_N both).

results.path: p0 site pair: UMA-suggested min xy vs saddle-region xy (on-N atop family)
results.method: DFT PBE/USPP constrained relaxations (QE 7.4.1-GPU, kgy RTX3090): adatom xy pinned / z free, 3x3 slab 136 at (bottom 2 bilayers frozen), ecut 60/480 Ry, k 2x2x1, MV 0.01 Ry, forc 1e-3 Ry/bohr
results.notes: min = p0_min4 (4-round carry chain, converged 07-15 18:05 KST); saddle = p0_saddle3 (converged 07-14 16:48 KST). Mid-run 'inversion' (converged saddle below UNconverged min) resolved on convergence -> normal ordering. 118.2 meV sits between presented fit (102) and Cui (133) -> consistent family. Two-point value is an estimate at fixed xy positions, NOT a full MEP; authoritative profile = KISTI 9-point drag (in progress). Cross-note: drag p0 (path-endpoint xy) was already >2 mRy below min4 while still unconverged -> UMA min xy likely offset from true minimum; final barrier judgment deferred to drag profile.

headline_comparison_DFT_SCF.interpretation: Same-protocol DFT shows LiC6 has ~6x higher Li adatom diffusion barrier vs Li3N (001), corresponding to ~10^4-fold slower Li lateral diffusion at room temperature. Robust against functional/pseudo choice since both systems use identical DFT settings.
headline_comparison_DFT_SCF.CAVEAT_2026-06-06: The Li3N 0.049/0.054 values came from a thin-slab UMA path now retracted. Proper-slab UMA gives 0.237 (hollow, wrong topology). For the Li3N vs LiC6 claim, use DFT/literature: Li3N(on-N) 0.133 vs carbon ~0.24-0.30 -> ~2x (NOT 6x, NOT 10^4 rate). UMA is unreliable for Li3N barrier (topology inversion).
headline_comparison_DFT_SCF.RESOLVED_2026-06-21: Full DFT CI-NEB now COMPLETE (li3n_001_pathA_dft_full): forward barrier 0.12 eV, matching Cui 2023 (0.133). Final ratio vs LiC6 (0.287 DFT-SCF) = 2.4x. Use headline_full_dft_neb_2026-06-21 below for the paper; this DFT-SCF block (li3n 0.049) is superseded.

headline_full_dft_neb_2026-06-21.lic6_method: DFT-SCF on UMA geometry (full LiC6 NEB not run; UMA over-smooths TS -> 0.287 is a slight under-estimate)

headline_full_dft_neb_2026-06-21.robustness: 2.4x is a conservative LOWER bound on the barrier ratio (LiC6 0.287 is DFT-SCF, would rise under full NEB). Li3N 0.12 is independently validated by literature (0.133).
headline_full_dft_neb_2026-06-21.paper_line: Full DFT CI-NEB gives a Li+ lateral migration barrier of ~0.12 eV on Li3N(001) — in quantitative agreement with the literature value (0.133 eV, Cui 2023) and ~2.4x lower than on LiC6 (0.287 eV), i.e. roughly 10^3-fold faster Li redistribution on the Li3N interphase, supporting homogeneous Li flux and dendrite-free plating in the anode-free configuration.

literature_sei_barriers_eV.ranking: Li3N has lowest barrier among 5 common SEI inorganics → most favorable for uniform Li redistribution at anode interphase.

paper_claim.system: AgNO3-derived nitrate-rich SEI for anode-free SSB
paper_claim.claim: Li3N interphase (from AgNO3 decomposition) provides a ~0.12 eV Li adatom migration barrier (full DFT CI-NEB; matches Cui 2023, 0.133 eV) — ~2.4x lower than lithiated carbon (LiC6, 0.287 eV), enabling ~10^3-fold faster Li lateral redistribution that homogenizes Li flux and yields dendrite-free morphology in the anode-free configuration.
paper_claim._updated_2026-06-21: Numbers corrected from the retracted 5.9x / ~10^4 (thin-slab UMA artifact) to the full-DFT-NEB result: Li3N 0.12 eV / 2.4x / ~10^3. See headline_full_dft_neb_2026-06-21 and li3n_001_pathA_dft_full.
supporting_figures: h-alt (E vs reaction coord, same protocol)
caveats_for_methods_section: Li3N forward barrier 0.12 eV is from full DFT CI-NEB and matches Cui 2023 (0.133 eV) within 13 meV.
LiC6 0.287 eV is DFT-SCF on UMA geometry (full LiC6 NEB not run); since DFT-SCF under-estimates the TS, the 2.4x ratio is a conservative lower bound.

The well-inclusive read of the Li3N path is ~0.18 eV (an on-N well at the path midpoint with metastable, slightly asymmetric end-sites); the quoted 0.12 eV is the forward well-to-saddle migration barrier.

The 'hollow' metastable site (+181 meV above on-N) is, upon coordinate analysis of the relaxed structure, identified as the on-Li site -- Li adatom sits 1.3 Å above a substrate in-plane Li at the 3-N centroid. Li+-Li+ electrostatic repulsion explains its higher energy. See hollow_site_identification_2026_06_09.

hollow_site_identification_2026_06_09._added_2026_06_09: Post-relaxation site identification, NOT in the original Cui 2023 paper. From hollow_s2 final ATOMIC_POSITIONS analysis of relaxed coordinates.
hollow_site_identification_2026_06_09.discovery: The site we were calling 'hollow' (the metastable basin at +181 meV above on-N) is geometrically NOT a vacuum hole between N atoms — it is the **on-Li site**, i.e. Li adatom sits ~1.3 Å directly ABOVE a substrate in-plane Li atom (which sits at the 3-N centroid in the Li2N termination plane).

evidence.substrate_in_plane_Li_xy: (0.000, 2.107) Å -- EXACT match with adatom xy
evidence.Δz_above_substrate_Li: +1.29 Å (adatom sits above substrate Li, no horizontal displacement)
evidence.three_N_centroid_check: N atoms at (0,0), (-1.825, 3.161), (1.825, 3.161) → centroid = (0, 2.107) = substrate Li xy = adatom xy. CONFIRMED: hollow = on-Li.

hollow_site_identification_2026_06_09.chemical_interpretation: Li adatom resting on top of a substrate Li(+) atom experiences Li(+)-Li(+) electrostatic REPULSION → destabilizes the site by +181 meV vs on-N (where Li adatom binds to N lone pair via charge transfer). This is consistent with the on-N being the well and 'hollow' being the metastable basin.

naming_correction.new_term: on-Li site (3-N centroid, occupied by substrate in-plane Li)
naming_correction.paper_writeup_recommendation: Use 'on-Li metastable site' or 'above-substrate-Li metastable site' instead of 'hollow' to be physically accurate. Cui 2023 also identifies this site but does not explicitly compute its energy (focuses on the on-N → bridge → on-N main path).

hollow_site_identification_2026_06_09.implication_for_UMA_failure: The previous interpretation that 'UMA places Li adatom at hollow (3-N geometric centroid)' was misleading. The actual UMA failure is that UMA predicted the on-Li site (above substrate Li) as a minimum or even global well due to packing-only chemistry, missing the on-N stabilization from N lone pair → Li 1s charge transfer. DFT correctly identifies on-N as the well because it captures this charge transfer.
